# Where Neutrinos Come From {#where-from}

## Cosmic accelerators {#accelerators}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### A black hole tears a star apart

{{< nh-video jet-launch variant="film-en" class="slide-video media-height-lg" style="--media-max-height: 620px;" controls=true muted=true playsinline=true preload="metadata" poster="../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/jets/jet_launch_en.jpg" aria-label="A black hole tears a star apart by tidal forces, the debris forms a disc, and the magnetic field launches a jet." >}}

::: {.media-caption}
Debris orbits computed, the magnetic “engine” shown schematically.
:::

### Active galactic nuclei

- A supermassive black hole sits at the centre of the galaxy.
- Gas falls onto it and swirls into an accretion disc.
- Magnetic fields take the rotational energy and launch a jet: a stream moving at nearly the speed of light.
- Gas keeps arriving for a long time, so the nucleus can shine for millions of years.
- If the jet points straight at us, such a nucleus is called a **blazar**.

::: {.media-caption}
[Blandford, Meier & Readhead, Relativistic Jets in AGN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.06025)
:::

### Gamma-ray bursts

- The collapse of a massive star or the merger of two neutron stars.
- Matter falls onto the compact remnant and for a short time powers an outflow at nearly the speed of light.
- The engine runs for seconds or minutes: a flash, not a steady source.

::: {.media-caption}
[P. Mészáros, Gamma-Ray Bursts](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0605208)
:::

::::::

## How does a jet produce neutrinos? {#jet}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### Star in the jet

{{< nh-video star-in-jet variant="film-en" class="slide-video media-height-lg" style="--media-max-height: 620px;" controls=true muted=true playsinline=true preload="metadata" poster="../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/jets/jet_star_en.jpg" aria-label="A star enters the jet; accelerated protons collide with its material and produce neutrinos." >}}

::: {.media-caption}
Scenario and calculation: [Barkov, Aharonian & Bosch-Ramon (2010)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.5252) · the film illustrates the idea: simplified gas model, schematic protons and neutrinos.
:::

### The chain

- The jet accelerates protons.
- A proton hits a nucleus of the gas or a photon.
- Pions are produced: $\pi^+$, $\pi^-$, $\pi^0$.
- Charged pions decay into muons and neutrinos, the neutral one into two gamma rays.
- A neutrino carries away about a twentieth of the proton energy.

::: {.question}
So what stands behind a 1 PeV neutrino? A proton of about 20 PeV, accelerated by the jet.
:::

::: {.takeaway}
- Where neutrinos are born, gamma rays are born too.
- But gamma rays can get stuck in the source, while neutrinos escape.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
[Ahlers & Halzen (2018)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.11112)
:::

::::::
